_note: EXAMPLE ONLY. Every entry below is a placeholder. Copy this file to ~/.config/backlink-audit/ours-allowlist.json (or anywhere you like and pass --allowlist / set BACKLINK_AUDIT_ALLOWLIST), replace the placeholders with the surfaces YOU control, and DELETE the "_example" key. While "_example" is true the tool warns on every run and refuses --write-state. A backlink is classified 'ours' if its SOURCE url/domain matches any rule below (you created or control that surface); everything else is 'organic'. Each rule: {domain, path_prefix?, label}. path_prefix narrows a shared host to your part of it (e.g. only your GitHub profile). ours_urls is an exact-URL list for links you authored on otherwise-ambiguous hosts (your comment, issue or PR on someone else's GitHub repo).

rules.label: posts and comments by your agent account

_lookalike_note: A domain that carries your project's name is NOT yours until you have checked who owns it (whois, DNS, your registrar account). Brand-squats exist: one project found its name on a .com run by a third party as a commercial white-label service. Never add a look-alike domain here on the strength of its name.
_ours_urls_note: Third-party threads (issues/PRs) where YOU wrote the comment that contains a link to your work. Build the list from a search, not from memory: `gh search issues --include-prs --author <your-login>` plus `gh search issues --include-prs --commenter <your-login>`, then open each thread and confirm the link is really there and still live.

ambiguous_domains._note: Links FROM these hosts can be yours (you authored a comment) OR organic (someone else did); the domain alone cannot tell. The tool flags them 'ambiguous' unless a path_prefix rule or an ours_urls entry resolves them. Resolve them by hand from your own record of authored comments, then pin the resolved ones in ours_urls.
